intro: Suan Son Beach is a quiet stretch of sand not far past Ban Phe, lined by a shady seafront road with pine groves on both sides — a different feel from the busier beaches · Banyan Resort @Rayong is a small bungalow-style resort tucked into a garden under the pines, just a few steps across the seafront road from the sea · It's an owner-run stay with 17 rooms that focuses on being clean, quiet, and easy on the budget, starting at around THB 800/night — a good fit for anyone who wants to fall asleep to the sound of the waves near the sea without paying a lot.

body.html: If you've ever driven through Ban Phe to catch a boat to Koh Samet and gone a little past the pier, you'll come to a seafront road shaded by rows of pines on both sides — that's Suan Son Beach, a quiet Rayong beach within the Ban Phe National Reserved Forest, only about 4 kilometers from Ban Phe market and roughly 29 kilometers from Rayong town · The beaches around here aren't as busy as many of the famous ones, but their charm is the calm and the shade of the pine groves that give the place a natural feel · And it's in a quiet area like this that Banyan Resort @Rayong sits — a small resort that isn't trying to be a luxury one, but is meant to be a clean, comfortable place to sleep at a price ordinary travelers can afford.

The first thing to understand is that Banyan Resort @Rayong is a small, owner-run stay with about 17 rooms, not a big chain resort with a fancy lobby or an army of staff · The rooms are bungalow-style and low-rise buildings spread through a garden, with large trees and the shade of the pines helping keep the atmosphere cool and pleasant · The point reviewers mention most often is the location right across from the beach — just a few steps across the seafront road and you're at the sea · For anyone coming to relax by the sea who doesn't need a pool or five-star hotel facilities, this is the perfect distance — you can wake up and walk along the beach right away without getting in a car · Being a small stay like this comes with its own upsides and limitations · The upside is that you get close, personal care — the owner remembers guests' faces, answers your questions personally, and the atmosphere isn't crowded like a resort with people coming and going all the time · The limitation is that the facilities are only what's essential — there's no fitness room, spa, or organized activities, so you have to plan your outings yourself · But for anyone coming to Rayong to relax quietly with the sea as the main event, these limitations are barely an issue, because most of your day will be spent on the beach anyway.

On the rooms, the resort has several sizes to choose from depending on your group · It starts with the Standard Room, a room with one large bed for two, ideal for couples or travelers who just want a clean place to sleep near the sea · Next is the Deluxe Room, which is more spacious and, in some rooms, has a garden view · And there are larger options like the Deluxe 4-bed room (1 large bed + 2 single beds) and the Large Room with garden view, which comfortably fit families or groups of friends · Every room has air conditioning, an LED TV, a balcony or private sitting area out front, an en-suite bathroom with a shower and water heater, free Wi-Fi, and free parking on-site · The decor is simple and clean, nothing flashy, but it matches what the price promises · What makes the rooms here nicer than many stays at the same price is the space out front · Because they're bungalows in a garden, many rooms have a balcony or sitting area that looks out onto the trees and the shade of the pines, great for sipping morning coffee or relaxing in the evening breeze · For families bringing kids, the 4-bed room is great value, because you get a lot of space at a lower per-person rate and don't have to split into separate rooms · One small tip: if you book during very hot weather, check that the air conditioning in your room works well and cools evenly, because some rooms in the garden get different amounts of sun — if you want the coolest, shadiest room, just tell the owner what you need when you book.

"The room was clean, very quiet, and you just cross the road to reach the beach. The owner and staff are lovely and helpful — at this price it's great value for a beachfront stay." — a summary of genuine reviews from several guests

The biggest strengths here, according to genuine reviews, are the cleanliness of the rooms, the peace and quiet, and the friendly service from the owner and staff · Many guests praise the rooms as cleaner than the price suggests, the beds comfortable, the air conditioning nice and cold, and the place so quiet you sleep easily, with none of the noise of beaches lined with pubs and bars · Because it's a small, owner-run stay, getting in touch or asking for help is easy and you get a quick reply · Another thing people mention is the convenience, since there's a 7-Eleven not far away, so finding food and supplies late at night is no trouble · Overall it has a "genuinely here to rest" feel that's more like visiting relatives by the sea than checking into a hotel.

Having talked about the upsides, we should be honest about the things to note too · Because it's a small, budget resort, there's no pool, no large restaurant, and no airport or pier shuttle service · If you're expecting the full set of facilities of a luxury resort, this may not be the answer · For breakfast, check with the resort first whether it's included in the rate, since some small stays don't include it, and it's worth heading out to a seafood restaurant around Ban Phe or one of the eateries along Suan Son Beach, of which there are a few · Some reviews mention an unpleasant smell from the bathroom drain in certain rooms, which is something you can run into at older seaside stays — if you hit this, tell the owner to deal with it or ask to change rooms · And since it's a small stay, the number of reviews on booking platforms is still limited, so read the score as a trend rather than a fixed number.

Location and getting around are an advantage here · Suan Son Beach is only a short drive of about 5 minutes from Ban Phe pier, the main pier for boats across to Koh Samet · That means you can use Banyan Resort as a base for a night before or after a trip to Koh Samet without having to rush back to Bangkok in a single day · From Bangkok, the drive to the Ban Phe–Suan Son Beach area takes about 3 hours along the motorway and the Rayong highway · Nearby there's also the Ban Phe Botanical Garden (Suan Son), Wat Khian Thong, and Laem Khao Laem Ya to drop by · There's free parking at the resort, ideal for anyone driving themselves.

As for what to do around the stay, Suan Son Beach suits a slow-paced break more than an active trip · In the morning, stroll along the beach under the pines, take in the sea breeze, then come back and chill on your balcony · Mid-morning, take a short drive into Ban Phe market for fresh seafood and to pick up well-known local products like fish sauce, shrimp paste, and dried seafood · If you have a full day, taking a boat from Ban Phe pier to Koh Samet as a day trip is easy, then coming back to sleep at Banyan Resort without lugging your bags to a pricier stay on the island · For nature lovers, the Ban Phe Botanical Garden and the surrounding pine forest offer a shady, walkable atmosphere · And for those who want a long beach to walk far on, Mae Ramphueng Beach in Rayong town isn't too far if you fancy a change of scene · The real appeal of staying in this area is that you get a quiet sea, without fighting for parking or jostling with crowds of tourists.

If we're weighing value, you have to place this in the budget beachfront category, not the luxury resort one · With prices starting at around THB 800/night and rising with room size and the season, getting to sleep just across the road from the sea in a quiet atmosphere under the pines is great value for a traveler who isn't hung up on luxury · Compared with hotels in Rayong town at similar prices that aren't on the beach, or resorts on Koh Samet that cost several times more · Banyan Resort @Rayong is therefore a choice for anyone who wants "the sea close by at an affordable price" rather than coming for resort facilities · Anyone who values calm, cleanliness, and a beachfront location will feel they got more than their money's worth at this price · Just think about it — if you stayed on Koh Samet in a similar room, you might pay double the room rate, plus the round-trip boat fare and the cost of eating on the island, which is pricier than on the mainland · Staying on the Suan Son Beach side and taking day trips by boat to the island therefore saves a fair bit on the overall trip budget, while still letting you experience both kinds of sea — the quiet mainland beach and the pretty island beaches · For a solo traveler or a couple on a budget, this is a value equation that works out well.

Things to know before you book: because it's a small, owner-run stay, during long holidays and high season (November–April) the rooms fill up very fast, so book ahead and message the resort directly to ask about room details, breakfast, and check-in times · Check-in is around 2:00 PM and check-out around 11:00 AM, so if you'll arrive earlier or leave later, let them know in advance · Suan Son Beach is a natural beach that's slightly steep with strong waves in some seasons, so be careful swimming, especially with children · And since it's in a quiet area, large restaurants may not be right next to the stay, so it's worth driving into Ban Phe, which has a variety of seafood restaurants and markets to choose from.

The friend-to-friend summary: Banyan Resort @Rayong is a simple beachfront stay on Suan Son Beach that's good value for anyone who loves quiet · It's not a resort you check into for infinity-pool photos, but a clean, quiet place to sleep near the sea with an owner who looks after guests in a friendly way · If you're looking for a base for a night before catching a boat to Koh Samet, or want a quiet Rayong beach trip on a light budget, this fits that need well at a price that's hard to beat for somewhere on the beach · Just set your expectations to match what a small stay can offer — clean, quiet, well-located — and you'll get a memorable seaside night's rest at an easy-on-the-wallet price.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Banyan Resort @Rayong, Suan Son Beach

faq.q: Where is Banyan Resort @Rayong, and how do you get there?
faq.a: It's on Suan Son Beach, Tambon Kram, Mueang Rayong, Rayong province, right across from the beach — cross the seafront road to reach the sea · From Bangkok it's about a 3-hour drive · It's around 5 minutes from Ban Phe pier and Ban Phe market, handy for catching a boat to Koh Samet, with free parking.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Banyan Resort @Rayong, and what room types are there?
faq.a: From around THB 800/night for a Standard Room · There's a Deluxe Room, a Large Room with garden view, and a Deluxe 4-bed room for families · Prices depend on room size and the season, so it's worth comparing several platforms and messaging the resort before booking.

faq.q: Does Banyan Resort @Rayong have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: No pool, since it's a small, budget resort · For breakfast, check with the resort first whether it's included in the rate · The Suan Son Beach area is quiet, with large restaurants over around Ban Phe, a short drive away.

faq.q: Can you swim at Suan Son Beach in front of the resort, and what's the atmosphere like?
faq.a: Suan Son Beach is a quiet, natural beach shaded by pine groves along the shore. You can swim, but the beach is slightly steep with strong waves in some seasons, so be careful, especially with children · It suits anyone who likes calm, beach walks, and relaxing by the sea away from the crowds.

faq.q: Who is Banyan Resort @Rayong best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, small families, and budget travelers who want to sleep near the sea in a quiet atmosphere · It works well as a base for a night before or after a trip to Koh Samet · It's not for those who need a pool, a large restaurant, or the full facilities of a luxury resort.

faq.q: What's the review score for Banyan Resort @Rayong?
faq.a: Around 8.3 from reviews on Trip.com (the number of reviews is still limited because it's a small stay) · What guests consistently praise is the cleanliness, the quiet, the beachfront location, and the friendly service from the owner — read it as a good indication of satisfaction in the budget beachfront category.
